_doc: Large batch L08 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): gila dragon, dune wyrmling, glass wyrm, desert and spurred tortoise, sand viper matriarch, rock python, grass snake, emerald python. New motifs live in motifs/large_L08.js (35, glyph/motion ids prefixed L08-; all 9 signatures bring a custom chain effect: gila plod with tail groove, wyrm humps breaching the dunes, hollow glass serpent with a prism glint, tortoise track, spurred charge, viper mother with her brood in file, python creeping in a straight line, collared snake swimming with a V wake, liana growing with the python on it) plus 4 composition motifs below. Every creature has its own signature motif and 8 of 9 keep it exclusive (barrel-coil, the rock python's, is lent to its sibling the emerald python for Squeeze). Reused only where the picture is truly the same: medium reptile motifs bead-hide and fat-tail (gila), venom-fang, venom-spit, scale-shingle, sidewind-track, tail-lash, smooth-coil; small musk-wave (grass snake musk) and glass-glint (glass armour). Sibling shares: needle-fangs (dune wyrmling -> glass wyrm Glass Fang), cactus-chomp, gopher-dig and shell-in (desert -> spurred tortoise). Every piece (unique, class and x0) has a hand note. Sonnet's flagged pieces are all given distinct pictures: gila x0 quake cracks vs u2 beaded stomp, b2 bead plate with glint; viper b1 sidewind tracks; glass b3 hot sand fling, x0 shattering blow, u1 glass splinters; spurred b3 dig dust, u1 gular ram; rock python b0 gape, b3 hiss gape in haze; grass snake b1 tail lash, b2 scale shingles, u2 smooth coils; emerald b1 liana tail, b2 scale mail, u0 barrel coil squeeze.

sand-fling.desc: a burst of hot sand grains flung out, glinting as they cool into glass beads

glass-splinter.desc: sharp glass splinters spat out in a fast run, a white glint flashing

bladder-splash.desc: heavy drops of a desert tortoise's stored water squirted out and splashing into a pool

hiss-mist.desc: round puffs of hissed breath blooming into a damp rainforest haze

desert-gila-dragon.notes: A gila monster grown to dragon size in the desert: pink and black bead scales, a fat stored-fat tail, a heavy head that bites, clamps on and grinds venom in rather than striking. Slow, stubborn, never lets go. Lands heavy with a shake.

u0.n: Gila Chew: the beaded jaws clamp onto the edge and grind, pale venom running down the jaw grooves and dripping off

u1.n: Bead Hide: rows of round bead scales line the edge and flip pink and black in a warning flash

u2.n: Slow Stomp: a fat five-clawed beaded foot lifts and slams down, cracks running out to the sides, dust jumping

u3.n: Lingering Bite: two arcs of tooth punctures stay on the edge, venom in the middle, ache rings throbbing out and out

b0.n: Hold-On Bite: the heavy beaded head lunges off the edge, clamps shut and hangs on grinding

b1.n: Slow-Turn Tail Whip: the fat banded tail swings slowly round off the edge and thumps

b2.n: Beaded Scale Plate: pale bead scales plate the edge, a glint rolling over the bumps

b3.n: Stubborn Spit: a beaded snout gapes and spits a fan of pale venom that drops off the edge

x0.n: Sudden Quake Slam: the dragon drops its whole weight; zigzag cracks split out from the edge and crust chunks jump

dune-wyrmling.notes: A young sand wyrm the length of a barn, pale as the dunes, that swims through the sand and breaches in humps; thin long needle fangs drip venom. Rises out of the ground onto its spot.

u0.n: Fang Snap: wyrm heads run the length of the edge, gaping and stabbing with two long thin needle fangs

u1.n: Sand Lance: the wyrm shoots along the edge under the sand, coils breaching and diving in a line, sand spraying

u2.n: Hiss: gaping heads blow S-shaped hisses off the edge with sand grains swept along in them

u3.n: Fang Dribble: the needle fangs hang open and venom beads dribble off their tips and splat below

b0.n: Long-Fang Stab: a head lunges off the edge and stabs with its thin long fangs

b1.n: Sand-Dive Tail: coils arch out of the sand off the edge and dive back in a puff of dust

b2.n: Sand-Sheen Scales: pale keeled scales shingle the edge, a sheen sliding over them

b3.n: Burrow Spit: a snout pokes out of the sand and spits venom that falls through a dust puff

x0.n: Barn Sweep: the barn-length body heaves out in one long arch and crashes back down, sand flying

glass-wyrm.notes: A long desert wyrm whose scales have fused to glass where lightning struck the sand: you see through its body, only the outline and a light glint, rainbows inside. Slides in low, sun-slow until it warms.

u0.n: Glass Lash: hollow glass coils lash out from the edge and drop back, a rainbow glint running through them

u1.n: Shard Spit: sharp glass splinters are spat off the edge in a fast run, a white glint flashing

u2.n: Fused Hide: hollow hexagon glass scales fuse along the edge, a rainbow band sweeping across them

u3.n: Slow Wake: glass eyes rise off the edge and open slowly in the sun, a slit pupil, a glint, warm rays

b0.n: Glass Fang: a clear head lunges off the edge, needle fangs of glass stabbing

b1.n: Glass Tail Shatter: glass tail tips whip off the edge, crack and fly apart into glinting shards

b2.n: Glass Armour: see-through outline plates line the edge, a light glint crossing them

b3.n: Glass Sandfling: hot sand is flung off the edge and falls glinting as it cools to glass beads

x0.n: Glass Waking Blow: a glass tail slams out and shatters on impact, shards and dust bursting

desert-tortoise.notes: Desert tortoise: a high dome of scutes with growth rings, elephant legs, a horny beak that crunches cactus; it digs burrows with shovel forelegs, stores water and waits months for rain. Very slow, very heavy landing.

u0.n: Shell In: tortoises along the edge pull head in, fold the scaly forelegs over the opening and shut with a tink

u1.n: Beak Nip: a horny beak lunges off the edge and crunches a notch out of a prickly-pear pad

u2.n: Dig Down: shovel forelegs dig out from the edge, domes sinking into burrows, sand thrown back, then they come back up

u3.n: Desert Long Patience: sun, then a cloud, then rain rises off the edge, and a beak sips the puddle at last

b0.n: Hill Chomp: a big beak pushes out from the edge, crunches the cactus pad and pulls back chewing

b1.n: Dune Cudgel: the high ringed dome shoves off the edge like a club, legs stamping

b2.n: Hilltop Shell: high domes settle along the edge like little hills, dust settling round them

b3.n: Crawl Trail Spit: a scared tortoise squirts its stored water; drops fall off the edge and splash

x0.n: Boulder Flop: a tortoise flops onto its back like a boulder, rocks with legs waving, then thumps over in dust

spurred-tortoise.notes: Spurred tortoise of dry grass and desert: a stout dry-yellow shell with a serrated rim and a forked gular horn under the chin, three big conical spurs on each thigh; males ram each other. Lands hard and fast for a tortoise.

u0.n: Spur Jab: thick scaly legs run along the edge, three conical spurs jutting out and jabbing

u1.n: Beak Spike: a stout tortoise charges along the edge and crashes the forked gular horn home

u2.n: Shell Hold: yellow shells line the edge, heads drawn in and spurred forelegs folded across, shut with a tink

u3.n: Slow Turn: the tortoise turns slowly in place and spurred legs bristle out all round the edge

b0.n: Spur Nip: a yellow beak lunges off the edge and nips a chunk out of a cactus pad

b1.n: Spur Lash: spurred legs kick off the edge, the spurs flashing

b2.n: Spur Shell: stout serrated shells brace along the edge, gular horns forward

b3.n: Spur Dust: spurred forelegs scrape out from the edge and kick up a cloud of dry dust

x0.n: Spur Stomp: a spurred leg stamps out from the edge and drops back in a burst of dust

sand-viper-matriarch.notes: The mother of the sand vipers: a heavy horned viper whose live-born brood peeks out of her coils and follows her sidewinding in a file; she ambushes from under the sand with a broad arrowhead and heat pits. Slides in sideways.

u0.n: Viper Fang: broad arrowhead heads with glowing heat pits rear and strike off the edge, venom drops falling

u1.n: Sidle: the mother and her brood slip sideways out from the edge and back, little heads popping up from her coils

u2.n: Brood Hiss: rows of tiny viper heads hang at spots round the edge, gaping and hissing, tied together

u3.n: Sand Sand Sting: horns and eyes in the sand, a bulge, a head erupts with a sting and sand rains down

b0.n: Sand Viper Fang: two curved fangs lunge off the edge, a venom bead swelling at each tip

b1.n: Viper Sidewind: slanted vipers step sideways off the edge leaving rows of J-shaped tracks

b2.n: Viper Sheen: keeled sand-coloured scales shingle the edge with a sheen sliding over

b3.n: Viper Spittle: a gaping snout spits a fan of venom that drops off the edge

x0.n: Viper Ambush: only horns and eyes show in the sand until the head erupts off the edge in a spray

rock-python.notes: African rock python of grass and hills: grey-brown blotches, thick as a barrel, basking sun-warm on boulders; sits and waits, senses warm prey with heat pits in its lips, strikes open-mouthed and squeezes. Slowest, heaviest landing.

u0.n: Rock Constrict: barrel-thick blotched coils heave out from the edge, tighten with a creak and drop back

u1.n: Warm Rock: sun-warmed boulders with a python loop draped over rise off the edge in heat shimmer

u2.n: Rock Blend: blotchy rocks spread out from the edge; one opens an eye and slides: it was the python

u3.n: Sitter Strike: a long head runs the edge, heat pits along its lip lighting one by one, then the strike

b0.n: Basking Strike: a python head lunges off the edge with its jaws wide on rows of hooked teeth and snaps

b1.n: Basking Tail-Whip: a thick blotched coil swings off the edge, heavy and slow

b2.n: Basking Cloak: warm boulders line the edge with the python draped over them, heat shimmering

b3.n: Basking Hiss: open jaws hiss off the edge in a warm haze and sink

x0.n: Basking Squeeze: stacked coils bulge out from the edge and clamp tight, dust squeezed out

grass-snake.notes: Grass snake of meadows and ponds: olive with a bright yellow and black collar behind the head; a strong swimmer, harmless, it sprays a foul musk and, if that fails, plays dead belly up with its tongue lolling. Bobs in like floating.

u0.n: Coil: along the edge the snake writhes, rolls belly up to show its chequered belly and goes limp, tongue lolling

u1.n: Strike: collared heads lunge off the edge, the yellow collar flashing, a red tongue flicking after

u2.n: Constrict: olive coils hang at spots round the edge and tighten, tied by thin lines

u3.n: Swim Away: the collared snake swims in an S from spot to spot round the edge and is gone

b0.n: River-Fang Strike: a snake swims off the edge out of the river, head up, collar bright

b1.n: Reed-Whip Tail: long thin olive tails uncoil off the edge and crack straight like reeds

b2.n: Green Scale Coil: olive keeled scales shingle the edge, a glint sliding along

b3.n: Musk Trail Spray: wavy musk lines curl up off the edge: the grass snake's stink

x0.n: Coil-Drop Crash: a collared head drops out of its coil, slams out from the edge and falls back

emerald-python.notes: Emerald python of the rainforest: vivid green with a row of white flecks down the back, it rests saddled over a branch in loose coils with its head in the middle, hangs down to strike with long front teeth and drops like a rope. Hangs above its spot, then drops.

u0.n: Squeeze: green coils hang stacked at spots round the edge and tighten, tied together

u1.n: Emerald Coil: coils saddle over a branch along the edge, white flecks on the back, the head resting in the middle

u2.n: Slow Swallow: long pythons rise off the edge, the lump of a meal sliding slowly down each body

u3.n: Rope Drop: the python drops off its branch like a rope, swings out from the edge and back

b0.n: Hanging Fang Strike: pythons hanging from branch stubs swing off the edge and bite with long front teeth

b1.n: Liana Tail Whip: a tail wound round a liana uncoils off the edge and whips straight with a crack

b2.n: Emerald Scale Mail: bright green scales shingle the edge, a glint sliding over

b3.n: Hiss Mist Spray: hissed breath blooms off the edge into a damp rainforest haze

x0.n: Constrict Hug: the saddled coils heave out from the edge, hug tight round the branch and drop back
